definition: In optimization, a gradient method is an algorithm to solve problems of the form min x ∈ R n f ( x ) {\displaystyle \min _{x\in \mathbb {R} ^{n}}\;f(x)} with the search directions defined by the gradient of the function at the current point.
details: Examples of gradient methods are the gradient descent and the conjugate gradient.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. Here is the short version: In optimization, a gradient method is an algorithm to solve problems of the form min x ∈ R n f ( x ) {\displaystyle \min _{x\in \mathbb {R} ^{n}}\;f(x)} with the search directions defined by the gradient of the function at the current point. The part that makes it sing: Examples of gradient methods are the gradient descent and the conjugate gradient. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. And that is Gradient method — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
